title: Phased Shearwave Deploy Log and Release Notes (Jan 2027) - Draft
content:
Overview:
This document is the working field notebook for the 'Shearwave' phased deploy of platform routing and model-variant fallback logic targeting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. It combines the preflight checklist, a compact rollout calendar (hourly + day-level), scripted watchlist for telemetry, rollback gating, and a release-notes draft intended for partner/customer-facing comms.

Release goal:
- Deploy routing switch to enable cheaper-variant fallbacks for high-latency tails while preserving 99th%-ile latency SLO for Platinum tenants.
- Validate autoscaler interplay with Dedicated pools under synthetic steady-state and spike workloads.
- Avoid any user-facing error-rate increase >0.05 percentage points vs baseline.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Staging environment mirrors prod-config w/ 48h warm cache.
- Canary VLAN is provisioned in us-west-2 only for initial waves.
- Ops on-call: Marcus (day), Priya (evening). Escalate to SRE lead Ethan if telemetry gates trip.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic shift):
- [ ] PR merged: platform routing + fallback (PR 1987) — author: Priya.
- [ ] DB migration: routing-matrix minor (non-blocking, reversible). Migration runbook: linked.
- [ ] Canary pool created with same node image and quantization flags.
- [ ] Load generator job created: shearwave-load-1 (ramp profile attached).
- [ ] Alerting: 99th latency, error-rate, model mismatch score, token-cost delta defined in alerts channel.
- [ ] Observability smoke: trace sampling turned on for new route paths; prefix caches instrumented.
- [ ] Feature flags: routing.fallback.enabled (off), routing.fallback.seeded (on for canary hosts).
- [ ] Rollout calendar posted to #release-ops and to stakeholders; support rotation assigned.

Warmup and canary plan (calendar):
Day 0 (staging validation, ~24h):
  - 09:00 verify migration rollback succeeds in staging.
  - 12:00 run steady-state generator for 6h; verify 99th latency delta < 5%.
  - 18:00 run spike simulations (2x peak) for 1h.
  - 20:00 sign-off meeting; produce staging snapshot.

Day 1 (canary waves, us-west-2):
  - 02:00 deploy to canary hosts (10 machines). health-check: /health+routing-status.
  - 03:00 start Wave A: 0.5% traffic (10m ramp). Observe for 30m post-ramp.
  - 04:00 if green, Wave B: 2% traffic (20m ramp). Observe 60m.
  - 06:00 Wave C: 5% traffic (30m ramp). Observe 120m.
  - 10:00 decision point: proceed to regional warmup or rollback.

Day 2 (regional warmup & dedicated validation):
  - 00:00 apply fallback to non-critical routing (10% of low-SLA tenants) for 2h test.
  - 04:00 Dedicated autoscaler dry-run (no traffic) verify scale policies.
  - 09:00 full-traffic soak on dedicated test pool (synthetic) for 4h.
  - 14:00 hold for manual review and stakeholder sign-off.
  - 16:00 start progressive ramp to 25% across regions (EU/US).

Rollout guardrails and telemetry gates (automatic checks):
- Gate L1: 5xx rate increase >0.03 -> immediate pause and page SRE.
- Gate L2: 99th latency increase >10% sustained for 15m -> autoscale suppression and manual review.
- Gate L3: model mismatch score (off-target responses) >0.8 delta -> auto-fallback to previous variant.
- Gate L4: token-cost per request increases >20% for >30m -> revert cost-affecting change.

Decision matrix (after each wave):
- All gates OK -> continue to next wave.
- Any gate tripped but contained and fixable in <45m -> pause, hotfix, re-run wave.
- Any gate tripped with unknown root cause or >45m remediation -> rollback to previous active routing config and open incident.

Rollback procedure (fast-path):
1) Flip feature flag routing.fallback.enabled -> false (control plane action).
2) Repoint traffic slices back to prior router tier (version pinned).
3) If control-plane flip fails, run emergency revert via infra-deployer (runbook: revert-deploy-quick).
4) Notify customers per comms template 1 (linked).

Communication plan (who notifies whom):
- Internal: #release-ops (real-time), #sre-alerts (escalation), daily standup summary to eng leadership.
- Customer-facing: For Platinum customers, steward owners (CS leads) notified at 0/6/24h. External status page updated if degradation observed.

Run-of-day watchlist (what to look for minute-by-minute during ramps):
- Health endpoints and routing-status junctions.
- 90th/95th/99th latency lanes broken down by model-size and seq-length.
- Token-cost per successful response and per error response.
- Cache-hit ratio for prefix/KV cache (expected warmup curve).
- Request routing entropy (to detect misrouting loops).

Operator checklist during each wave (quick-actions):
- Confirm deploy completed on all nodes in the wave.
- Validate no schema drift in function/tool-calls aggregator.
- Snapshot traces for a 10m window and push to shared trace folder.
- Post a wave status update in #release-ops with metrics snapshot.

Known risks and mitigations (engineering notes):
- Risk: Fallback path may increase token usage for long-context queries. Mitigation: soft-throttle large seq-length requests (configurable).
- Risk: Dedicated autoscaler cold-starts can momentarily increase latency. Mitigation: pre-warm instances when ramp >10%.
- Risk: Billing spike for alpha customers. Mitigation: cost-monitoring alert set and quota guard for trial tenants.

Release notes (draft for customers / partners):
Title: Shearwave rollout — smarter routing with economical fallbacks (Jan 2027)
Summary: This release introduces a staged routing fallback that routes requests to compatible, lower-cost model variants when latency tail risk is low, and falls back to higher-quality variants when needed. The change reduces expected per-token cost for many workloads while maintaining our latency SLOs.
What’s changed:
- New routing policy: routing.fallback with seedable thresholds and per-tenant overrides.
- Telemetry: traceable routing decisions (new trace span: routing.choice).
- Autoscaler: improved scale-prewarm hook for Dedicated pools.
- Safety: automatic rollback on latency or error gates; customer opt-out via per-tenant flag.
Known issues (working list):
- Some long-sequence conversational flows may see slightly longer first-token time during fallback decisions. Rolling mitigation: adjust prefix-cache TTL and priority.
- Edge case: function-calling responses occasionally strip optional metadata when using variant A-quota — tracked in RWINF-3470.

Post-release tasks (owners and deadlines):
- 24h: Incident triage + short retro (owner: Marcus Chen).
- 72h: Telemetry enrichment (owner: Priya Nambiar) — add additional routing labels.
- 7d: Cost impact analysis and unit-economics update (owner: Product Analytics).
- 14d: Finalize customer-facing release notes and knowledge base article (owner: Customer Success).

Open action items (quick backlog):
- Add synthetic jitter-resilience test to continuous deployment suite. (PR follow-up: platform/pr-1999)
- Confirm per-tenant opt-out UI works for Dedicated customers behind feature toggle.
- Schedule a small-customer pilot for the EU region in Feb (CS outreach: pending).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a living document. If you add a checklist item or adjust a gate, update the commit log below and ping the release thread.
- If you are assigned an owner action, put your name next to the item and update status as you progress.

Commit log (working):
- 2026-12-15: Initial draft and preflight checklist (Ava).
- 2027-01-04: Added telemetry gates and refined rollback fast-path (Marcus).
- 2027-01-10: Updated release notes and action owners; added linked PR/JIRA references (Priya).

End of document.
